task_instance: Register and exercise the /meta command handler described by the skill: in the telegram_agent bot codebase, add a handler so that a user typing '/meta fix the rate limiting bug' spawns a Claude Code Agent SDK session with working directory set to the telegram_agent project and returns the session's reply back into the Telegram chat. Verify end-to-end by issuing one /meta command and seeing a response.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is a working Telegram /meta command that receives the user's text, spawns a Claude Code Agent SDK session, and returns the reply in Telegram. Exercising/verifying this inherently requires two networked services that are unreachable on this air-gapped workstation: the Telegram Bot API (to receive the command and deliver the reply) and the Anthropic model service that the Claude Agent SDK calls. It also requires a Telegram bot token (credential) that is not available. Compounding this, the telegram_agent project the skill modifies (expected at ~/ai_projects/telegram_agent, with src/bot/handlers/claude_commands.py and src/bot/bot.py) is not present, and the python-telegram-bot library needed to build/run the handler is not installed and cannot be installed without a package registry (no network). Per the task rules I did not write a stub/mock of the Telegram runtime or Claude session and did not fabricate a bot token or responses.
evidence: Skill repo (skills/r163) contains only meta/SKILL.md; no bundled scripts. SKILL.md defines a COMMAND HANDLER registration requiring edits to src/bot/handlers/claude_commands.py and src/bot/bot.py of the telegram_agent project and use of ClaudeCodeService.execute_prompt with a custom cwd. Checks run from the work directory: 'ls ~/ai_projects/telegram_agent' -> No such file or directory (target project absent); 'python3 -c import telegram' -> ModuleNotFoundError (python-telegram-bot not installed, cannot install offline); claude_agent_sdk imports OK and the claude CLI exists, but both still require network access to the Anthropic model service plus credentials to run a session, and the Telegram side requires the Telegram Bot API network plus a bot token. No deliverable could be produced or verified end-to-end offline.
